[00:00] Teacher (EN): Good morning, everyone. Let's start with a question. What does a plant need to stay alive? Hands up, please. Yes, Ayo?

[00:09] Student (EN): Water!

[00:12] Teacher (EN): Water, good. What else?

[00:16] Student 2 (EN): Sunlight. And soil.

[00:20] Teacher (EN): Sunlight and soil, and air too. Where have you seen plants growing near your home?

[00:27] Student 3 (EN): By the road, and my grandmother grows tomatoes.

[00:32] Teacher (EN): Lovely. Today we will learn the parts of a plant and the job each part does. Say it with me: parts of a plant and their jobs.

[00:42] Student (EN): Parts of a plant and their jobs.

[00:46] Teacher (EN): Look at this plant. I'm going to slide it gently out of its pot. What parts can you see?

[00:53] Student (EN): Leaves! And a flower. And the green part in the middle is the stem.

[01:00] Teacher (EN): Yes. And down here, these thin hairy threads?

[01:05] Student 2 (EN): Roots.

[01:08] Teacher (EN): Roots. The roots have two jobs. They hold the plant firmly in the soil so the wind can't blow it over, and they drink up water from the soil. Sam, what would happen without roots?

[01:22] Student 3 (EN): It would fall over when the wind blows, and it would dry up because it can't drink.

[01:28] Teacher (EN): Exactly. Now, yesterday I put this celery stick in a cup of red water. Look at the cut end. What do you notice?

[01:37] Student (EN): There are little red dots! And red lines going up the celery, all the way to the leaves.

[01:44] Student 2 (EN): So the water went up from the cup?

[01:48] Teacher (EN): Those lines are tiny tubes. The stem carries water from the roots up to the leaves, just like a straw.

[01:57] Teacher (EN): Now the leaves. Leaves catch sunlight and use it, with water and air, to make food for the plant. That's why leaves are flat and wide, to catch lots of light. Some plants even turn their leaves to face the sun, like sunflowers. And the flower? The flower makes seeds, so new plants can grow.

[02:19] Student 3 (EN): Teacher, is that why bees go to flowers? To help make the seeds?

[02:26] Teacher (EN): Yes! Bees carry tiny yellow powder from flower to flower, and that helps the flower make seeds. Great thinking.

[02:36] Teacher (EN): Let's label my drawing on the board. Lina, come and write roots. Tomi, stem. Sam, leaves. And Ayo, flower. Well done, give them a clap.

[02:47] Teacher (EN): Now, groups of four. Each group has part cards and job cards. Match each part to its job, and lay the pairs out in a line on your desk so I can see them when I come round. Five minutes, starting now. Group two, please sit together, not across the room.

[03:06] Student (EN): Teacher, does carries water go with stem or roots?

[03:11] Teacher (EN): Good question. Roots take water in, the stem carries it up. So carries water goes with the stem.

[03:19] Teacher (EN): Time's up. Let's check together. I point, you tell me the job. This part?

[03:26] Student (EN): Roots! They hold the plant in the soil and take in water.

[03:32] Teacher (EN): And this one?

[03:35] Student (EN): Stem! It carries water up to the leaves, like a straw.

[03:40] Teacher (EN): And these?

[03:43] Student (EN): Leaves! They make food from sunlight.

[03:47] Teacher (EN): And the last one?

[03:50] Student 2 (EN): The flower makes seeds, so new plants can grow.

[03:55] Teacher (EN): Brilliant. Now your exit slip. Write one plant part and its job, with your name, and pass it to the front.

[04:04] Teacher (EN): Thank you, I have them all.

[04:07] Teacher (EN): For homework, find a plant at or near your home, draw it in your science notebook, and label the roots, stem, leaves and flower. Well done today, everyone.
